name: Background Demo
tagline: A task the backend owns: start it, close the window, come back to its complete current state.
description:
Background Demo is the reference example for **backend-owned tasks** — work that an Executa runs outside any invoke.

The page only triggers and reads:

1. **Start** — one `tools.invoke` registers a task and returns its id at once.
2. **Leave** — close the window or switch to another app. The Executa keeps going: every step is a reverse RPC issued outside any invoke, served with the Executa's background credentials.
3. **Come back** — the page asks the Executa for its tasks and renders their complete current state, including rows that are still running.

The task doubles as a **capability health check**: each row exercises one family of reverse RPCs in the background — storage, object storage, web search / fetch / image search / image fetch, LLM sampling, an agent session, embeddings, image generation, text to speech and host upload (video and music are off by default).

The Executa also writes a storage heartbeat when its process starts and every five minutes: work that no user action triggers.

Every check spends a small amount of your CU.
_comment_bundled_executas: Executas that ship inside this app. `anna-app apps publish` publishes each one first, then substitutes its server-minted tool_id into every `bundled:<handle>` reference in manifest.json (in memory — the file on disk is never mutated). The `background-check` handle maps to ./executas/background-check-python.
